chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: An oath is not valid regarding the making permissible of the forbidden, nor the forbidding of the permissible, nor the severing of family ties.

key_terms.تَحْرِيمُ حَلَالٍ: making the permissible forbidden — rendering unlawful what God has allowed
key_terms.تَحْلِيلُ حَرَامٍ: making the forbidden permissible — rendering lawful what God has prohibited
key_terms.قَطِيعَةُ رَحِمٍ: severing of family ties — breaking the bond of kinship, considered a grave sin in Islam
key_terms.يَمِينٌ: oath/sworn vow — a solemn affirmation sworn in God's name, a legally significant act in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: Is an oath valid if it involves making the forbidden permissible or cutting family ties in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a legal ruling that oaths (yameen) sworn with the intent to legalise what God has forbidden, prohibit what God has permitted, or cut off family ties are void and not binding. This teaching clarifies a core principle of Islamic jurisprudence: an oath cannot override divine law or the moral obligations of kinship. The audience of jurists and companions understood that such an oath would represent an abuse of a sacred institution, and so it carries no legal or moral weight.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The swearing of an oath is not allowed regarding the permitting of a Prohibition, nor for the prohibiting of a Permissible, nor for cutting off of a relationship’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
It is not permissible to take an oath to make an unlawful matter lawful, a lawful matter unlawful or to cut off good relations with relatives.’”
